classification.difficultyReason: Apply depreciation and compound-interest formulas to the same initial cost, and interpret the depreciation multiplier as a total percentage reduction.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A computer shop spent $\$320\,000$ installing alarms at its premises. If it depreciated them at $20\%$ p.a., find the estimated value after six years, and the percentage reduction of value over that period. Give the value to the nearest cent and the percentage reduction to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
The annual value multiplier is $1-0.20=0.80$.

$$\begin{align*}A_6&=320\,000(1-0.20)^6\\A_6&=320\,000(0.80)^6\\A_6&=\$83\,886.08\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage reduction}&=(1-0.80^6)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage reduction}&=73.7856\%\\\text{Percentage reduction}&\approx73.8\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The business borrowed the money to install the alarms, paying $8\%$ p.a. compound interest for the six years. How much did it owe at the end of the six years? Give your answer to the nearest cent.
